architecture.mechanism: Uncontrolled regeneration — the exothermic oxidation of deposited particulate matter (PM) — releases heat that can raise temperatures uncontrollably; the paper identifies control methods (accurate soot prediction, safe regeneration strategy) that constrain this exothermic process and limit thermal overload on engine components.
architecture.intervention: Integrate the paper's accurate soot prediction with a safe, reliable regeneration strategy into the engine/aftertreatment control unit so that PM oxidation is initiated and modulated only within a verified safe thermal window, preventing the uncontrolled exothermic temperature excursion that can produce localized overheating and engine block hole formation.
architecture.expected_effect: Regeneration heat release stays bounded, peak metal temperatures and thermal stress in the engine block fall below the threshold that drives hole formation, and the abrupt popping/overheating failure mode is suppressed.
architecture.falsification_test: Instrument a 2020 Camry-class engine block and DPF with thermocouples and pressure sensors; compare (a) baseline control vs. (b) soot-prediction-governed regeneration across repeated low-speed (15 mph) duty cycles; if peak block temperature, thermal gradient, and regeneration exotherm duration show no statistically significant reduction in (b), the mechanism is falsified.
